items.title: US Fintech Weekly: Fiserv Bounces Post-Earnings, Crypto Brokers Suffer, And Federal Agencies Prepare Innovation Guidelines
items.summary: A Democratic sweep is pulling Bitcoin prices lower and weighing on crypto brokerages.

items.title: Trader suffers eight liquidations as panic selling grips markets
items.summary: A broad market selloff triggered more than $1 billion in crypto liquidations.

items.title: Robinhood Sinks 10%, SoFi Down 8% as Bitcoin Slides and Fintech Stocks Sell Off
items.summary: Key TakeawaysRobinhood shares fell 10% today in a crypto-led selloff, pulling SoFi, Block and PayPal lower too. Robinhood fell harder than PayPal and Block because most of its revenue still comes from customers’ trading.

items.title: Market Selloff Hits Financial Stocks. Why Banks, Brokerages Are Caught in the Crossfire.
items.summary: Shares of financial services companies as varied as Robinhood, Webull, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley fell sharply on Thursday.

items.title: Circle Sinks 10% as Crypto Stocks Slide and Mizuho Calls Q3 “Uneventful”
items.summary: Key TakeawaysCircle shares fell 10% today as crypto stocks, Robinhood included, slid with the market and seven firms cut their price targets. $182 million of Circle’s $865 million in third-quarter revenue came from a one-time presale of its ARC token.

items.title: Robinhood Sinks 12%, SoFi Tumbles 9%, Affirm Drops 8% as Bitcoin Slides and Democratic Congress Weighs on Fintech
items.summary: Crypto is bleeding and a new Congress is circling, but the sharpest fintech selloff is not hitting every name equally. Why are PayPal and Block holding up while the growth darlings take the heat, and who in Washington is setting the stakes?

items.title: Bitcoin tumbles below $76,000 as post-election stock rally fades
items.summary: Bitcoin tumbled below $77,000 on Thursday as investors moved out of riskier assets amid a broad sell-off in stocks.

items.title: Anthropic Is Going Public, and You Might Be Able to Buy the Stock at Its IPO Price
items.summary: The artificial intelligence company intends to allocate a portion of IPO shares to customers of some of the nation’s largest brokerage firms.
